card: This pull request replaces the Boost.Test library with a custom, in-tree header-only test runner that implements expression decomposition and compatibility shims for existing assertion macros. Today, writing and debugging unit tests requires navigating inconsistent Boost assertion macros that often fail to print operand values on failure, while maintaining Boost.Test incurs build-system workarounds in Guix and depends. Replacing Boost.Test has been a long-standing goal discussed in issues dating back to 2016 (#8670, #34666), driven by dependency reduction and recurring platform bugs like signal stack overflows (#36045). The PR touches over 160 files, but the majority of edits are mechanical scripted-diff replacements of include headers.

enables: Incremental migration of test files from legacy BOOST_* macros to native CHECK and REQUIRE macros without merge conflicts.

evidence: Author points to historical issues surrounding Boost.Test maintenance, citing RFC #34666, issue #8670, and signal stack bugs like #36045.

Author demonstrates inconsistent failure output between BOOST_CHECK, BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL, and BOOST_TEST where custom Bitcoin types fail to compile or omit value diagnostics, contrasting it with expression decomposition in the proposed runner.
Build simplification removes Boost.Test compile flags and Guix stack workarounds (commit 53c89d1f17).
problem: Bitcoin Core's unit test suite relies on Boost.Test, which has fragmented assertion macros with inconsistent failure diagnostics, lacks custom output formatting for Bitcoin types, and introduces dependency overhead including Guix and build-system workarounds.
scope_notes: The PR introduces a new ~1,200 line test runner framework in src/test/util/framework.h. Over 150 files are touched purely by a scripted diff replacing the Boost test include with the new framework header.
summary: Replaces the external Boost.Test unit test runner with an in-tree, header-only testing framework implemented in test/util/framework.h. It provides expression decomposition for assertion failures, adds macro shims for existing BOOST_* assertions to minimize churn, and drops the Boost test component from the build system, depends, vcpkg, and Guix.
